purpose: jenscolt's leg (left and right) as parameters: the blade's skin from a spine and a few control sections, so it bends onto N0's leg path by its spine alone; the right leg is the left one mirrored. Pilot (2026-11-20) adopted as the method; fidelity at the default.
pass_criterion: leg-blade within the default fidelity (tools/mesh_ref.py) of L_leg1 both ways with its skin from ≤ 60 numbers; build.py --edit bends it onto N0's right-front blade curve (spine within 0.5 mm of it) and makes the length +10 % and bow +3 mm variants, every one a valid closed solid; the judge scores ≥ 0.70 against the mesh render
must_have: leg-blade's skin from a spine curve (BLADE_SPINE, ≤ 5 control points) and ≤ 8 control sections interpolated along it (≤ 60 numbers in all for the skin); the seam grooves, socket and eye placed relative to the spine so they follow a bend
leg-arm's neck on a spine of ≤ 5 points (hub, gears and tab rigid at its start), so it bends onto N0's inner and upper leg path; same fidelity gate (Morante, 2026-11-20: N1 bends both parts)

build.py --edit writes out/edit-*.stl and images/edit-demo.png: (a) the blade bent onto N0's right-front blade curve (cad/mockup/n0.py leg_shape with P0, imported, never copied) in N0's frame at its S, (b) length +10 %, (c) bow +3 mm; prints FAIL for any variant that is not one valid closed solid or, for (a), whose spine is more than 0.5 mm from N0's curve
build.py --sweep as in v1 (S 0.65, thickness and arm section 0.8x / 1.2x)
a fidelity-vs-sections table in datasheet.md: blade p95/max with 4, 6, 8 control sections (and v1's 26), so Morante sees the trade-off
the right leg (leg-blade-r, leg-arm-r) from the same model by a mirror parameter, never a second model; its fidelity against jenscolt's R_leg1 / R_leg2
must_not: build.py never reads an STL or uses trimesh: the meshes are read only by the gates and by the designer's probes (scratchpad)
no warp or morph of mesh vertices

build_time.source: Morante, 2026-11-20: both parts, coarse STL + STEP
